prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a foreground curved table surface extending from about 0.3 m at the bottom edge to 0.9 m at its far edge, holding two side-by-side laptops roughly 0.5–0.7 m in front of the camera wearer and about 0.1 m apart, with a chair back behind them at ~1.2 m and a background desk, monitor, and double doors at 3–5 m. The camera wearer's right hand is in the lower-left foreground at ~0.3–0.4 m, while a second person sits to the right at ~0.5–0.8 m (partially cropped at the right frame boundary) facing left toward the laptops rather than toward the camera wearer, with their left arm reaching ~0.5 m forward onto the right laptop and their right arm tucked slightly behind it. Both laptops and a small object (face mask) to the right of the second laptop are within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person on the right, whereas a third person partially visible at the far-left edge (~1.5–2 m away, facing right) is out of reach; the foreground hands occlude parts of the laptop bases, and the laptops occlude the lower half of the chair behind them. Across the five frames, the scene layout and person distances remain largely static except in frame 4, where the camera wearer's right hand lifts slightly closer to the camera and tilts upward with two extended fingers toward the left laptop screen before returning to rest on the palm rest in frame 5. The depth map makes the continuous distance gradient across the table surface and the depth separation between the overlapping arms on the right much clearer than RGB alone, though it is unreliable on the far-left person, the background monitor, and the right-hand person's head/head-mount in frames 2–4 where depth values bleed into the dark background or saturate.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map delineates the two foreground laptops (~0.5–0.7 m away, left and center-left), the chair directly behind them (~1.2 m), the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-left foreground (~0.3–0.4 m), the seated person on the right (~0.5–0.8 m, cropped at the right edge and facing left toward the screens), and the partially visible person at the upper-left edge (~1.5–2 m, facing right). Both laptops lie within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the right-side person, with the camera wearer's hand overlapping and occluding the lower edge of the left laptop, and the right-side person's extended left forearm overlapping the lower-right corner of the center-right laptop. Across the five frames, the masks remain mostly stationary except for the camera wearer's hand mask, which shifts upward over the left laptop keyboard in frame 4 as two fingers point toward the screen before settling back down in frame 5, and the far-left person's head, which becomes slightly more visible in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the segmentation map explicitly isolates individual object boundaries such as the chair crest behind the laptops and the separate mask for the camera wearer's hand versus the right-side person's body. However, it is unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the folded white face mask on the table (~0.7 m away, to the right of the second laptop) as a 'cup', labels the background wall/window region as a 'tv' and the right-side double doors (~3–4 m away) as a 'refrigerator' in frames 1 and 5, fragments the left-edge tablet into 'laptop'/'tv'/'cell phone', and only detects the 'dining table' surface in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks 2D skeletal keypoints in an otherwise black frame, consistently localizing two hands within arm's reach in the foreground: the camera wearer's right hand on the lower left (~0.3–0.4 m away, resting on the left laptop) and the right-side person's left hand to its right (~0.5–0.6 m away, resting on the second laptop's touchpad, about 0.25 m from the camera wearer's hand). In frames 3 and 4, yellow upper-body and facial keypoints appear on the right side (~0.6–0.8 m away), showing the right-side person's head above their shoulders facing left toward the laptops (not looking at the camera wearer) with their elbows bent and forearms extending forward onto the table. While the right-side person's left hand stays stationary in a pinched posture on the touchpad across all five frames, the camera wearer's right hand transitions from a curved resting posture on the keyboard in frames 1–3 to an elevated two-finger pointing posture aimed upward toward the left screen in frame 4, then back to a flat resting posture in frame 5. This map reveals exact finger joint articulations and the hidden wrist-to-shoulder arm geometry of the person on the right in frame 4 more explicitly than the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable for full-scene understanding because it completely misses the far-left person (~1.5–2 m away), fails to detect the right-side person's head and torso in frames 1, 2, and 5 due to severe right-edge cropping and self-occlusion, and provides no spatial information about the table, laptops, or background layout.
